issue.description:
Gate: [OMN-13640](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-13640) AC-1

`ledger_lock.py` is the mutex that makes the rolling work ledger a usable
coordination surface for concurrent lanes. A roll that drops rows out of git, or
that shifts the line numbers other gates resolve by, breaks that surface while
reporting success. Both halves below were measured on 2026-09-17.

## Defect 1: the roll writes its archive UNTRACKED

A cap-crossing append rolled 928 rows out of `docs/tracking/ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER.md`
into a new 1.5 MB `docs/tracking/archive/ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER_2026-09-17-split.md`,
which it created as an **untracked** file.

Committing exactly what rule 19 says to commit, the one path the lane edited:

```
python3 scripts/commit_lock.py -m "..." -- docs/tracking/ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER.md
```

produced a commit reading `1 file changed, 8 insertions(+), 928 deletions(-)`
with no archive in it. The rows were on disk but outside git, one
clean-untracked or one worktree prune away from being gone.

Nothing in `ledger_lock.py`'s output said a roll had happened; the append printed
normally. It was caught only by reading the commit stat, where 928 deletions for
a four-row append is visibly wrong. Repaired as omni_home `79f7ead2d1`.

## Defect 2: the roll shifts every line citation above the split

The same roll removed 926 lines from the top of the live file, so every
`ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER.md:<line>` citation written before it is now off by 926. Two
measured examples: the operator's qwen hold ruling was `:4311` and is now
`:3385`; the "Grant both" consent row was `:4367` and is now `:3441`.

This is not cosmetic. Line citations are resolved mechanically:

| resolver | citation form |
| -- | -- |
| `omniclaude/plugins/onex/hooks/lib/credential_rotation_guard.py` | `ROTATION-CONSENT: <path>:<line>` (regex at `:222`, resolved at `:838-862`) |
| `omnibase_infra/scripts/apply_application_database_acl.py` | `--consent-citation <path>:<line>` (`:307`) |

**Correction to the brief:** there is no third resolver validating `consent=` in
CLAIM rows. `ledger_lock.py` carries no `--consent` flag, because rule 18's
mechanical enforcement ([OMN-16728](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-16728)) is still unshipped, so `consent=` in a CLAIM
row is prose today. The two above are the complete set.

A roll can therefore make a pending rotation consent unresolvable, or worse,
make a citation resolve to a **different row** than the one the author meant.
The rotation guard fails closed on a non-consent row, so the realistic harm is a
refused legitimate rotation plus a confidently wrong diagnosis.

## Acceptance

AC1 -- a roll never leaves rows outside git: it either stages and commits the
archive together with the ledger, or refuses to roll and says so. -- falsifier: a
test that drives a cap-crossing append in a throwaway git repo and asserts that
after the roll, `git status --porcelain` reports no untracked file under the
archive directory; paired with a test asserting the refusal path names the
archive it would have written.

AC2 -- the roll announces itself on stdout, so a caller cannot commit a roll
without knowing one happened. -- falsifier: a test asserting the cap-crossing
append's stdout names the archive path and the rolled row count, where the
pre-change output was silent.

AC3 -- a roll appends a banner row recording the offset it introduced, of the
form `ROLL: lines above <N> shifted by -<K>`, so a line citation dated before the
roll can be resolved deterministically after it. -- falsifier: a test that rolls a
seeded ledger and asserts the banner row carries the row count actually removed
and the first kept line number, checked against the file's own before/after line
counts rather than against a constant.

AC4 -- citations may be written and resolved as
`ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER.md@<row timestamp>`, which a roll cannot invalidate because
the timestamp travels with the row into the archive. -- falsifier: a test feeding
the timestamp form to the rotation guard and asserting it resolves to the same
verdict as the equivalent line form, plus one asserting it still resolves after
the cited row has been rolled into the archive.

AC5 -- both existing resolvers accept the timestamp form, and the line form keeps
working unchanged so no pending citation is invalidated by this change itself.
\-- falsifier: the rotation guard's own test suite run green with both forms, and a
test asserting an existing line-form citation is still honoured.

AC6 -- the committed `omnibase_infra/scripts/ledger_lock.py` and the gitignored
`omni_home/scripts/ledger_lock.py` mirror stay byte-identical. -- falsifier:
`shasum -a 256` over both paths reported in the PR evidence, equal before and
after.

## Why (a) plus the banner, and not the refusal-to-roll option

The brief offered "refuse to roll while any row cites a line the roll would move"
as an alternative to the banner. It is rejected: a citation is a bare
`<path>:<line>` string, so "cites a line the roll would move" is not decidable
from the file. Every integer in every row above the split would have to be
treated as a possible citation, which makes the roll refuse essentially always
once the ledger is busy, and the cap then stops working. The banner is
deterministic and costs one row.

## References

* Ledger FRICTION row, lane `omn17819-venv-reconciler-revert-1552`, in
  `docs/tracking/ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER.md`
* omni_home `79f7ead2d1` (the repair), and the
  `8 insertions(+), 928 deletions(-)` commit stat (the falsifier)
